decisions.reason: Uses the manifest to show fs-ext@2.1.1 is pinned by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, and the log to show its node-gyp configure build install script fails because Visual Studio/MSVC is missing.

Cites the top-level flock import in lease.ts. Explains that --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install to module load, because the native entry must still load on Windows, so the service cannot boot.

Separates the Windows path, acquireLockHandleWin32 with a named semaphore, from POSIX flock. Concludes the native flock is dead code on Windows, which is why the module only needs to load there. Keeps the semaphore on Windows and native flock on POSIX.

Follows the node-pty precedent with a pnpm patch for fs-ext. The install script skips node-gyp on win32, and the entry gets a guarded pure-JS flock fallback with a callback shape. Registers the patch under patchedDependencies and allowBuilds, and proposes install, load, boot and POSIX checks.
States clearly that Visual Studio is not installed and upstream is not changed. Uses the repository-managed patch applied at install time.
Cites DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 in full and ties it to the fs-ext Windows install failure and the patch recipe.

caps.reason: The plan explicitly rules out installing Visual Studio.
--ignore-scripts is rejected, and the plan makes the entry loadable through the patch.
The plan uses a local pnpm patch and explicitly avoids forking or releasing upstream.
The Windows semaphore is kept, and POSIX keeps real native flock. The no-op fallback only applies when the binding is missing on Windows.
